title: Choose the visual world for the showtimes console
question: The roll assigned the Lobby Letterboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each comp shows the AI import review open over the schedule.

options.label: Lobby Letterboard
options.thesis: The schedule is set like the lobby board: every approved change is a letter you slot in by hand.
options.viewport: A felt-black band holds the theater's lineup in white board letters; below, the review lists each proposed change as a board line, approvals slot letters in.
options.risk: Board caps are slow to read; the felt must stay a band and a signature, never the whole working surface.

raised.raise: Two inks only on the board, felt and letter; state is carried by letter color sets, never by greys.
The felt groove pitch is the layout grid; table rows and review lines snap to it.
One thing owns each screen: the board on the console, the change list in review.

options.label: Galley Proof
options.lineage: newspaper showtime listings proofed before press
options.thesis: The partner's drop arrives as a proof of the listings; the agent marks it in blue, you initial each mark in red, only red prints.
options.viewport: A dense listings column with blue agent marks and margin notes; each mark carries a red initial box the operator ticks before applying.
options.risk: Proof-room editorial is a familiar look; it fails the moment it slides into hairline-serif magazine styling.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: One yellow band always says where you are and the single next decision: upload, review, apply.
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band names the theater and the next step; the review below reads like a departures list of decisions.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity of state; loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Yellow fatigue if it leaks beyond the one band.

options.label: Day Score
options.thesis: The day as a score: auditoriums are staves, each showtime a block as long as its runtime, changes notated beside it.
options.viewport: Auditorium columns with runtime-length blocks; the review overlays proposed moves and archives as notation on the score.
options.case: Shows overlaps and moved showtimes better than any table; loses on familiarity for daily list work.
options.risk: The table view still has to exist beside it; two views to maintain.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The schedule as a strobing data field.
options.risk: Operators would not recognize their work in it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither the audience nor the task reads through it.
options.kept: Two-ink discipline: state by color set, no greys.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible grid.
options.risk: A type exercise, not a working tool.
options.kept: A visible grid that everything snaps to.

options.label: Factory Catalog
options.viewport: A black field with one plot.
options.risk: Coded labels hide information operators need.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coding names fights clarity.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.kept: Each theater keeps fixed personal furniture.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern ops console, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, filters over a sortable table, the review as a side sheet of proposed changes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every admin tool by design.
